exoplasim.geometry: 3 liquid water layers of 0.02, 0.48 and 1.0 m, ACTIVE only at nlandwcol 1
exoplasim.what_it_reads: evaporable_mm from the emitted states as the column capacity `dwmax` in metres of water, and the per-layer usable shares grouped onto its three water layers as the capacity SPLIT `dsoilwfc`
exoplasim.note:
`dwmax` is a capacity, not a thickness. The geometry above is the running one -- `surface.land_water_column` declares `layered` at these three layers -- and the 0.5 m boundary in it is not a free choice: it is exactly this file's own 500 mm upper and 1000 mm lower grouping, which is the only cut at which the climate column and the ecology column share a boundary. LSHY-5 needs them to share it, because two columns cannot agree about frozen soil across geometries that do not meet. The 0.02 m cut ABOVE it is `surface_layer`, and it moves no boundary either column reads: 0.02 + 0.48 is 0.5.
`evaporable_mm` and not `awc_mm`, and the difference is one layer deep. A root cannot reach the water between air dry and the wilting point and a bare drying surface can, so the surface layer's capacity is cut from air dry and the column's is the sum. LPJ-GUESS reads `awc_mm`, which is unchanged. See `surface_layer`.
THE CAPACITY SPLIT IS A FIELD, on the same footing as the capacity it splits. It is not one shape: measured over this build's land cells the upper layer's share sits at the geometric 500/1500 wherever the profile is uniform -- the quarter of land where the regolith fills the column, plus the cells whose weathered bedrock is at the capacity ceiling -- and rises to nearly nine tenths everywhere the regolith contact and the bedrock fraction reweight it. So it crosses as surface code 2290, one record per water layer, derived from the SAME per-layer usable shares the `awc_mm` column is the integral of: the split and the capacity are one arithmetic rather than two that agree today. `dsoilwf` in `landmod_nl` is what a cell no field covers takes. WORLD-VJBZ.
Its five SOIL TEMPERATURE layers are a THIRD geometry, 0.4/0.8/1.6/3.2/ 6.4 m, which reaches 12.4 m and shares no boundary with either water column; landmod maps between them by midpoint.

lpj_guess.geometry: 15 physical layers of 100 mm, grouped 5 upper and 10 lower
lpj_guess.what_it_reads: the emitted states and the per-layer usable shares, through its driver file; and sand, clay, silt, pH, organic carbon and the mineral-reactivity columns from the soil map
lpj_guess.note: `vesperinput.cpp` multiplies each layer's awc, wp and wsats by the usable share emitted here, and rescales the two aggregate figures to match. It moves no layer boundary and no root, so a shallow-regolith cell has the same rooting depth as a deep one with less water in it. The share is READ: the weathered-bedrock vertical rule is evaluated once, by the enforcing script, and was implemented in both places until WORLD-OF6N.

pedology.what_it_writes: the soil map's texture, regolith depth, weathered-bedrock fraction, organic and andic columns, which this contract's states are derived FROM. Its `awc` column is pedology's own declared endmember mixture, cut at the column base under WORLD-7702, and no consumer reads it: it is the alternative the report costs the adopted closure against.

retention_closure.name: clapp_hornberger
retention_closure.note: Named so the choice is legible and comparable. Cosby et al. support texture as a predictor of MEAN hydraulic behaviour and emphasise that large residual variance remains within texture classes, so the closure carries the shape and the uncertainty cases below carry the spread.

declaration_mutations.first: geometry: 12 layers of 0.1 m reach 1.2000000000000002 m, and column_base_m is 1.5
geometry: the rootable base is below the column base. A root cannot draw from water the column does not carry
geometry: vadose_base_m and aquifer_boundary.contact_depth_m are two names for one contact and they disagree
states: ordering names 'turgor', which is not a declared state
state field_capacity: does not say whether it depends on gravity. That is the one question this contract exists to answer the same way twice
potential_convention: the wilting point is a suction and is negative in this contract's sign convention

potential_convention: the drainage length gives an Earth field capacity suction of 3236.2 Pa, and Cosby's 10^2 cm of water is 9806.65 Pa. The two must agree or the drainage length is not what Cosby measured at
retention_closure: family 'empirical' is not one of the two implemented families. A closure with no family stated is the thing this block exists to prevent
uncertainty: cases must be applied coherently. Drawing each layer independently averages the spread away over 15 layers and reports a false precision
aquifer_boundary: transmissivity must be scaled separately. A vadose unsaturated conductivity is not an aquifer permeability

consumer_comparison.exoplasim_source: what dwmax WAS: the pedology awc column converted mm to m. It is now the emitted states file's awc_mm column on the same terms
consumer_comparison.reading: The two fields correlate because both start from related texture and depth. They are not the same capacity: one is a declared endmember mixture with additive organic and allophane terms, the other is a Cosby retention inversion with no andic term and no bulk density. That is the disagreement the adopted case ended.
consumer_comparison.soil_carbon_note: the checked-in map carries zero soil carbon everywhere, so the organic mixing paths of both derivations are inactive and the divergence reported here is the MINERAL one alone

cosby_air_entry_clamp.criterion: 1.58 * sand + 0.63 * clay < 0.17 is where the air-entry clamp binds; unclamped the inversion returns a field capacity above saturation there
cosby_air_entry_clamp.verdict: the CODE keeps this right, and the map has never needed to. WORLD-NGA10 clamped both heads at the air-entry value in get_mineral; WORLD-OF6N moved the derivation into contract_states and the clamp with it, so the closure cannot return a field capacity above saturation for any texture. No cell of this map is inside the region, so the clamp changes no current soil property; the margin is what says how far that is from being true by accident.
cosby_air_entry_clamp.bound_is_conservative: the line is derived at Cosby's own field-capacity suction. The adopted suction is larger, so the region where the clamp binds is strictly smaller than this

gravity_field_capacity_shift.direction: down, on every cell. Stronger gravity drains a column to a drier state at equilibrium; the wilting point is a plant pressure and does not move, so plant-available water falls.
gravity_field_capacity_shift.applied_note: APPLIED. WORLD-OF6N adopted the contract read literally, so the emitted states evaluate field capacity at rho_w * g * L with this planet's gravity and every consumer installs them. Pedology's declared endmember capacities are Earth field observations and are no longer what any consumer reads.
gravity_field_capacity_shift.bracket_note: an UPPER BOUND on the size of the effect and adopted as one: it holds the Clapp-Hornberger exponent fixed while gravity moves, so it is the whole of the shift a gravity-invariant curve can produce, and the within-texture-class spread Cosby reports is larger than the shift -- `uncertainty_cases` measures both moves in the same capacity. A declared limitation of the adopted value, not a reason to leave the states at Earth's suction: the shift moves every cell the same way, so unlike a scatter it does not average out over the map.

frame_consistency.reading: the two consistent frames are one number and the frame-mixed variant is a different one. The wilting point does not move under a change of gravity, because it and the air-entry value are both invariant pressures recorded as Earth heads and their ratio is what the closure reads. Field capacity is the only state whose defining pressure carries gravity.

adopted.name: closure_at_vesper_suction
adopted.what: the contract's named closure at the suction its own potential convention declares, rho_w * g * L at this planet's gravity. The closure is named and field capacity is declared as a drainage equilibrium over a declared length, so this is the contract read literally and no part of it is a new choice
adopted.deleted: pedology's endmember volumetric capacities, its additive organic term and its allophane term as the source of any consumer's capacity; soilinput.cpp's get_mineral Cosby inversion; and vesperinput.cpp's apply_regolith_depth rescaling, whose rule is now layer_usable_fraction here
adopted.limitation: the gravity shift holds the Clapp-Hornberger exponent fixed while gravity moves, so the adopted field capacity is an UPPER BOUND on how far a gravity-invariant retention curve can fall.
adopted.uncertainty: Cosby's within-texture-class residual spread, carried in `uncertainty_cases` and declared in the contract's uncertainty block. It is larger than the gravity shift, and that comparison is measured there rather than asserted here.

closure_at_earth_suction.what: the same closure evaluated at Cosby's own field-capacity suction, which is the pressure the shipped LPJ-GUESS code used. Not adopted: it reads the contract's closure and ignores the contract's potential convention, which declares field capacity as a drainage equilibrium and therefore at this world's gravity

pedology_endmember_mixture.what: pedology's declared endmember volumetric capacities with its additive organic and allophane terms. Not adopted, and not a symmetric option: it is not a retention curve at all -- no saturation, no air entry, no exponent -- so taking it would have replaced the contract's named closure and left saturation and matric potential with nowhere to come from

adopted_case.andic_is_not_the_disagreement: the allophane term LPJ-GUESS has no equivalent of contributes a median of nothing and a p90 of a few per cent of pedology's capacity, against a median absolute gap between the two derivations of tens of millimetres. What separated them is that the declared endmember capacities and the Cosby retention inversion are different numbers for the same texture, not that one carries a material the other does not. The adopted closure carries no allophane term either, so the andic hydraulic effect is now a DECLARED absence rather than a disagreement between two consumers
adopted_case.not_measurable_here: the change in land runoff ratio and in E over R. Both need a paired baseline, pedology/scripts/probe_runoff_response.py needs a climatology to back-solve potential evaporation from, and config/planet.yaml declares baseline_climatology null. On this build the capacity change is costed and its climate consequence is not available at all
adopted_case.not_execution_verified: nothing on the LPJ-GUESS side. It does not build on this tree until a baseline climatology exists, so every LPJ number here is a transcription of the vendored source evaluated offline

uncertainty_cases.source: cosby1984 Table 4, the S.D. rows: the within-texture-class residual spread of the same parameters whose means are the adopted central case
uncertainty_cases.applied: coherently across all layers and all properties in one case
uncertainty_cases.is_an_envelope: low and high are the per-cell extremes over the corners of the one-sigma box in b, log Psi_s and Theta_s. Cosby reports the three residual spreads separately and no correlation between them, so this is a bound on what the spread can be worth and not a percentile of a distribution. A correlation, if it were published, could only narrow it.
uncertainty_cases.installed_note: the emitted states are the central case and every consumer installs that. A case is a states file away: `contract_states` takes the deviates and nothing downstream of it knows which case it read.

against_the_gravity_shift.note: the gravity shift is one-signed and moves every cell the same way, so it does not average out over the map; this spread is a scatter and does. They are not interchangeable and the comparison is of magnitude only.

air_dry_overdraw_mm.what: the water the surface layer can give up that a real soil would hold by adsorption at the ambient humidity. `air_dry_water_content` is declared zero, so the overdraw is the sub-wilting increment times theta_ad over theta_wp, an unknown fraction under one; the BOUND and its direction are what is known

split_invariance.what: the column total and the runoff under a two-layer and a three-layer partition of the same total capacity, driven by one flux sequence through landcolumn.f90's own cascade
split_invariance.why_it_matters: the surface layer buys a store that empties in a day instead of a season and costs the water budget nothing. If this fails, it costs something, and the cost is not a rounding error.

saturation_endpoints.note: the surface layer's own mapping. It differs from the thermal one in the lower endpoint only, because its capacity is cut from air dry and the layers below it are cut from the wilting point.

albedo.note: `landmod`'s `getalb` under `nwetsoil = 1` mixes the staged dry and wet band pairs on this saturation. The mixing form is Sadeghi, Jones and Philpot (2015): linear in the Kubelka-Munk transformed reflectance and therefore NOT linear in the albedo, which is the CLM form this row started from and which no longer describes the shape between the ends.

dust_emission.reads: a gravimetric water content, through this layer's bulk density and thickness
dust_emission.note: The emitting depth is DUST-17's and is not this contract's to set. What is settled here is that whatever depth it declares is a reading off this profile: `aeolian/config/dust.yaml` states the gravimetric conversion once and reaches the model as the single namelist constant `dustwcv`, and the surface layer is what that conversion applies to. Until DUST-17 lands, that file's `moisture.soil_depth_m` is 0.5 and the two rows are reading different depths off the same column, which is legal and is why the depth is a per-consumer field here.
